name: Fingal
intro: Fingal sits quietly between Rye and Cape Schanck on the Peninsula's ocean-coast flank, and it is the kind of place that earns its reputation through what happens there rather than through what it calls itself. Peninsula Hot Springs has made it a pilgrimage destination for a particular kind of weekend — thermal pools, early morning mist off the coast, a round at Moonah Links, and nothing much else demanding your attention. The Cape Schanck lighthouse is fifteen minutes south. The back beaches are wild and within reach. Fingal rewards the visitor who wants comfort rather than activity.
factualLede: Fingal is a coastal village on the Mornington Peninsula's ocean-coast edge, 90 km from Melbourne, home to Peninsula Hot Springs and adjacent to Moonah Links golf resort and Cape Schanck.

heroImage.alt: Ocean coast near Fingal and Cape Schanck, Bass Strait

tldr: Fingal is the Peninsula's wellness and golf destination — Peninsula Hot Springs is here, Moonah Links is here, and Cape Schanck is a short drive south.
Best for: thermal wellness weekends, golf stays, couples who want luxury without Sorrento's crowds.
Signature experience: a morning thermal soak at Peninsula Hot Springs, then a round at Moonah Links, then nothing.
Two nights minimum — Fingal is about slowing down, not covering ground.
notFor: anyone who wants to walk to dinner
worstTime: peak summer weekends — hot springs are crowded and book out weeks ahead
signature: The Peninsula's thermal heart — where the weekend slows all the way down.
skip: Expecting a village. Fingal is a destination, not a town.
bestDay: Hot springs at 7am before the crowds, late breakfast at the resort, afternoon round at Moonah Links, dinner in-house.
insiderNote: Book Peninsula Hot Springs at least three weeks ahead for weekend sessions. Weekday thermal visits are calmer and cheaper.
